A1.justification: Both PDFs contain the same study and complete 38-page document, including the checklist, UKLO examples, and generated-puzzle appendices. Text extraction, image checks, and page rendering support a reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original o1 puzzle-solving experiments, GPT-4o/o1 writing-system experiments, generation of 18 puzzles, and human evaluation of selected puzzles (Sections 4–5, Tables 2–5, Appendix C).

after.justification: v2 retains the same original experimental outcomes, including model scores, generated puzzles, and human-evaluation results in Sections 4–5 and Appendix C.

M1.justification: The puzzle-solving procedures and GPT-4o/o1 generation methods are identical, including the zero-shot, one-shot, and few-shot prompts incorporating puzzle-design principles (Sections 4–5).

E1.justification: Both retain LINGOLY, the UKLO writing-system puzzles, the Greek alphabet probe, Greek/Gujarati/Spanish generation, and Swedish/Kabyle human-evaluation controls. No dataset, language, task, or scenario changes.

E2.justification: Table 2 retains the human and previously reported Claude Opus comparisons with o1. Table 3 retains humans, GPT-4o, and o1; the generation comparison also retains both models.

E3.justification: Exact-match scoring, topic/difficulty aggregation, sample sizes, prompt-example counts, and the three-evaluator study with a 15-minute limit per puzzle remain unchanged (Sections 3–5).

E4.justification: The language-knowledge error analyses, Greek alphabet probe, prompt-setting comparisons, and generated-puzzle validity analyses are identical, including their supporting appendix examples (Sections 4.2, 4.4, and 5.3–5.6).

E5.justification: Table 4 and Section 5.3 retain the same averages and Fleiss's/Cohen's kappa agreement reporting. No repeated-run, seed, confidence-interval, or significance-testing information changes.

E6.justification: All reported scores, findings, and generated outputs are identical. For example, Table 3 retains Round 2 scores of 45.2 for humans, 15.6 for GPT-4o, and 24.5 for o1; Tables 4–5 and Appendix C also match.

T1.justification: Section 5.1 retains identical puzzle-design principles and validity criteria. No mathematical definitions, assumptions, derivations, theorems, or proofs are added, removed, or revised.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion are unchanged, retaining the claims about LLM puzzle-solving capabilities, writing-system difficulties, and generation of valid but relatively simple puzzles.

C2.justification: Interpretations concerning reliance on prior language knowledge, language-independent generation, and puzzle validity remain identical. Section 7 retains the same limitations concerning data, coverage, creativity assessment, and expert availability.

D1.justification: Puzzle-to-image processing, prompt/example descriptions, evaluator instructions, resource information, and appendix outputs are unchanged. No implementation or reproducibility details are added or removed.

R1.justification: Section 2, the reference list, and statements positioning the work relative to earlier puzzle-solving and generation research are identical.

P1.justification: The first-page stamp changes from v1/26 Sep 2025 to v2/17 May 2026, and PDF title metadata swaps 'Solve and Generate' to 'Generate and Solve'. The printed title, prose, and section structure remain unchanged.

P2.justification: Figures, tables, captions, appendix displays, and page layout are unchanged. Pages 2–38 render identically; the only visible difference on page 1 is the version/date stamp.

improvement.justification: The scientific content, experimental evidence, explanations, limitations, and appendices are identical. The version/date stamp and title-metadata edits provide no meaningful improvement or deterioration in the paper's overall quality.
